bullets.title: PLTR: Citi upgrades to Buy, $200 PT on 149% US Commercial growth
bullets.body: Citi upgrades PLTR to Buy with $200 PT (from Neutral) after Q2 US Commercial revenue surged 149% Y/Y with record $2.1B TCV. FY26 revenue guidance raised $500M; US Commercial growth guidance lifted to 134% Y/Y; FCF margin 63%; 220 deals above $1M closed. UBS also highlights 93% total revenue growth and $3.37B TCV in Q2; stock +10.1% after-hours.

bullets.title: SNAP: Strong 2Q beat, +10% AH; Citi maintains Neutral at $6.50 PT
bullets.body: SNAP Q2 revenue $1.60B (+18.9% Y/Y), ~4% above consensus; adj. EBITDA $250M (~30% beat); DAUs 493M above 486.7M est; global ARPU +13% Y/Y. Q3 guidance $1.70-$1.74B slightly above consensus. Spotlight engagement +115% more posters YoY; Specs AR glasses launch fall 2026 seen as major long-term opportunity. New share repurchase program announced; Citi maintains Neutral at $6.50 (6.5x 2027 EV/EBITDA).

bullets.title: Mag 7 hyperscalers surge; AMZN hits $3T market cap, Mag 7 P/Es at 2-std-dev discount
bullets.body: JPM Spec Sales notes Mag 7 P/E multiples trading 2+ standard deviations below 2018-2023 mean, implying ~30-56% upside to fair value. AMZN +4.6% crosses $3T market cap; MSFT +4.7%; META +6.1%; GOOGL +4.9%. AWS backlog grew 150% YoY to ~$1.7T vs 80% capex growth. Hyperscalers on pace for ~$900B CapEx in 2026, $1.5T in 2027 per Morgan Stanley estimate.

bullets.title: ON Semi beats Q2, AI data center revenue to >2x in 2026; expands Nvidia MGX role
bullets.body: ON reports Q2 EPS $0.74 vs $0.71 est; revenue $1.60B vs $1.59B; gross margin 39.3% vs 37.6% year-ago. Q3 EPS guided $0.81-$0.93 vs $0.83 est; Q3 gross margin guided 40-42%. AI data center is fastest-growing business with TAM raised from $12.2B to $47.5B by 2030. Expanded role in NVDA MGX platform.

bullets.title: EA: F1Q bookings miss at $1.35B vs $1.50B Street; FCF -$318M
bullets.body: UBS maintains Neutral on EA after Q1 net bookings of $1.35B missed Street's $1.50B; GAAP EPS $1.56 beat on timing. Live services +3% (Apex offset by lower FIFA UT), full game +9% (FC/UFC). FCF disappointed at -$318M vs UBS estimate of +$104M — the clearest negative in the print.

bullets.title: FSLR +10.3%, VST/TLN/OKLO/NNE rally; S232 polysilicon tariff decision within 2 weeks
bullets.body: Power/utilities sector outperformed on AI data center demand theme. Notable movers: NNE +10.5%, FSLR +10.3%, SMR +7.0%, OKLO +6.2%, BE +6.1%. ROTH Capital expects Section 232 polysilicon tariff decision within 2 weeks; stringent tariff would be direct positive catalyst for FSLR's US domestic manufacturing thesis.

bullets.title: RBLX: Macquarie downgrades to neutral, PT cut to $37; JPM initiates neutral at $40
bullets.body: Macquarie downgraded RBLX to neutral from outperform and cut PT to $37 from $80. JPMorgan also assumed coverage at neutral with $40 PT. Separately, Citi maintains Buy: Week 31 CCUs of 16.3M imply 3Q26 bookings of $1.69B, above the high end of company guidance ($1.65B) and consensus ($1.61B).

bullets.title: INTU: Truist downgrades to hold, PT cut to $350 from $410
bullets.body: Truist analyst Arvind Ramnani downgrades INTU from Buy to Hold, cutting PT to $350 from $410 (implies ~10% upside from ~$318). FactSet consensus target is $443.52, suggesting a meaningful divergence from Street.

bullets.title: AAPL: Phillip Securities downgrades to reduce, $290 PT; UK data encryption legal challenge filed
bullets.body: Phillip Securities downgrades AAPL to reduce from neutral with a $290 PT implying 5% downside; FactSet consensus $328. Separately, Apple filed a legal challenge with the UK Investigatory Powers Tribunal against government access to encrypted iCloud backups.

bullets.title: NVDA: Jefferies cuts Rubin shipments to 1M units for FY26; HBM4 cost doubles to $31-32/GB
bullets.body: Jefferies lowers Rubin GPU shipments to 1M units for FY26 (from 1.5M) but notes higher Blackwell orders keep total FY26 shipments roughly flat. Key margin risk: HBM4 cost rising to $31-32/GB vs prior $20/GB estimate; RUBIN GPU price projected to jump to $78-80K. AMD CoWoS allocation raised to 300k wafers in FY27.

bullets.title: CRWV initiated Overweight at $151 (76% upside); NBIS initiated Neutral at $224
bullets.body: Piper Sandler initiates CRWV at Overweight with $151 PT implying 76% upside from ~$86; FactSet avg target $138. NBIS initiated at Neutral with $224 PT implying only 5% upside from ~$213; FactSet avg $270.

bullets.title: META: White House AI meeting Tuesday; Threads #1 on App Store; stock +13% in 4 days
bullets.body: META and GOOGL invited to White House Tuesday to examine AI framework per Politico. Threads ranked #1 on the App Store. META recovered all post-earnings losses and is up ~13% from a 4-day-ago buy signal. Stock +6% on the session as hyperscaler AI ROIC narrative improves.

bullets.title: APP: eCommerce client growth decelerating; 3Q26 avg store count tracking 11.1K
bullets.body: Citi Buy note shows AppLovin eCommerce clients at 10,837 (+1.2% WoW) but US stores fell 0.2%. 3Q26 YTD average weekly growth at just 1.0% vs 2.2% in 2Q26 and 3.1% in 1Q26, implying avg store count of ~11.1K for 3Q26. HK growth likely reflects dropshipper churn, not real net adds.

bullets.title: INTC IR call: 14A ramp in 2028, revenue 2029; foundry loss at $8B run-rate improving
bullets.body: UBS IR call notes: INTC beat driven by better yields/cycle times; 18A continues to beat, 14A tracking near 22nm performance. Foundry running $8B annual loss but improving; 14A revenue majority in 2029. EMIB getting strong validation; SK Hynix joining for scale. Key near-term constraint is supply/wafers/substrates over next 18 months, not roadmap.

bullets.title: TKO: Citi Buy, Q2 beat, FY26 raised 1% above consensus; $225 PT
bullets.body: Citi maintains Buy on TKO; 2Q26 revenue $1,547M and adj. EBITDA $650M both ~1-2% above consensus. FY26 guidance raised to $5,775-5,825M revenue and $2,275-2,305M EBITDA (1% above consensus mid). PT $225 implies 24% total return at 20x 2027 EV-Normalized EBITDA.

bullets.title: ORCL: CACI partnership win on $400M federal HRIT modernization contract
bullets.body: CACI International named as one of Oracle's partners on the U.S. OPM Federal HRIT Modernization contract — a 10-year, ~$400M award to modernize and consolidate federal HR systems into a single cloud platform. Other partners include Baker Tilly and Deloitte. ORCL +9.2% on the session.

bullets.title: AXTI: InP shortage creating supply constraints; positioned as world's largest supplier
bullets.body: Multiple posts flag AXTI as world's largest InP (Indium Phosphide) substrate supplier with high gross margins, capacity expansion underway, and supply unable to keep pace with demand — primarily driven by AI/photonics applications. AXTI broke above its 200-day EMA on the session.

bullets.title: MU: Citi removes from 90-day upside catalyst watch on mixed memory peer earnings
bullets.body: Citi removed Micron from its 90-Day Catalyst Watch citing mixed 2Q results from memory peers. No rating change disclosed, but the removal signals diminished near-term conviction ahead of MU's own reporting cycle.

bullets.title: GS TMT desk: most-loved plays AMD/ANET/WDC/DDOG/NET; analog semis lagging despite ISM beat
bullets.body: GS TMT desk notes NDX up ~590bps in 3 days with V-shaped recovery. Most-loved earnings plays: AMD, ANET, WDC, DDOG, NET. Most out-of-favor: SNAP, UBER, HUBS (now reversing post-print). Analog/power semis lag despite ISM Manufacturing 4-year high at 55.6: MPWR -5%, TXN -3%. SOX now only 20% above 200-dma vs 80% in June.

bullets.title: TSLA: European EV registrations surging; France +86% YoY, Denmark +52% YoY in July
bullets.body: Tesla registrations surged 86% year-over-year in France and 52% in Denmark in July, suggesting strong European market share momentum heading into 3Q26 deliveries.
